podcast.title: What's on your plate?

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: What is one dish from your country every visitor must try? Guess: who in this episode cannot eat spicy food — Leyla or Sam?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. And I'm a little hungry, because today's topic is food and culture.
[laugh] Perfect timing. Sam, you came to my family's house last month. What did you eat?
Plov! Your mum's plov. Rice with saffron, meat, chestnuts, dried fruit... honestly, it was the best homemade meal of my year.
In Azerbaijani cuisine, plov is like a king. There are more than forty kinds.
Forty! And the portion she gave me was huge. Then she gave me a second one.
Of course. If your plate is empty, a mother thinks you're still hungry.
I learned that the hard way. [chuckle] I couldn't move for an hour.
So what's a staple food in England? Something people eat every day?
Bread and potatoes, I think. Simple food. But I love trying new things when I travel.
Even very spicy food?
[sigh] That's my weak point. In Thailand I ordered noodles that the waiter called 'a little hot'.
And?
I cried for ten minutes. Lesson learned: never bite off more than you can chew.
[laugh] Poor Sam. For me, the most interesting part of travel is trying a local delicacy, even a strange one.
Like what?
In Japan I tried raw sea urchin. The main ingredient is... well, the sea urchin. It tasted like the ocean.
Brave. Okay, let's talk about table manners. They're different everywhere, aren't they?
Very. Here we serve tea to guests again and again. In some countries you shouldn't finish everything; in others you should.
So the easy rule is: watch what your host does. It's a piece of cake.
Nice. And here's some food for thought: when you share a meal, you share a culture. Your question for your next SpeakLab call: what dish would you cook for a guest from abroad?
Not too spicy, please! See you next time.
[laugh] Bye for now!

questions.q: What is the episode mainly about?
options: Food, eating habits and manners in different cultures
questions.why: They talk about plov, spicy food, delicacies and table manners.

questions.q: Why couldn't Sam move for an hour after dinner?
options: Leyla's mum gave him two huge portions
questions.why: "The portion she gave me was huge. Then she gave me a second one."

questions.q: What happened to Sam in Thailand?
options: He ordered noodles that were far too spicy for him
questions.why: The waiter said 'a little hot' and Sam cried for ten minutes.

questions.q: Leyla did not like the sea urchin she tried in Japan.
questions.why: She says it tasted like the ocean, but not whether she liked it.

questions.q: Sam says: never "bite off more than you can chew". What does it mean?
options: Never try something too difficult for you
Never eat food you don't like
questions.why: The noodles were much too spicy for him — he took on more than he could handle.

questions.q: What is Sam's 'easy rule' for table manners in a new country?
questions.why: "The easy rule is: watch what your host does."

talk: What dish would you cook for a guest from abroad — and why that one?
What is a table manner in your family that a visitor might not know?
